memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Phinehas son of Eleazar, the priest, and the leaders returned to Canaan from their meeting with the Reubenites and Gadites in Gilead and reported to the Israelites. They were glad to hear the report and praised God. And they talked no more about going to war against them to devastate the country where the Reubenites and Gadites lived. And the Reubenites and the Gadites gave the altar this name: A Witness Between Us — that the Lord is God. — Josh 22:32-34 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The good news travels home, and the whole assembly is glad. They praise God, and all talk of war ceases. Then the eastern tribes give their altar a name that captures the heart of the whole story: "A Witness Between Us — that the Lord is God."

What a fitting end. The very altar that had nearly caused a war now stands as a lasting sign of unity and shared faith. Every time someone passed it, its name would preach a sermon: the Lord is God, and we all belong to Him together.

This is how God works — He takes what could have destroyed His people and, through humility and truth, turns it into a testimony of grace. The near-disaster became a monument. The misunderstanding became a memorial to unity.

The whole chapter leaves us with a beautiful picture of the church God desires: a people who love Him, who take both holiness and one another seriously, who seek the truth before assuming the worst, and who guard their unity for the sake of generations to come. Jesus prayed that His people would be one, so that the world would believe (John 17:21). May our lives together bear that same name — a witness between us that the Lord is God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Has God ever turned a near-disaster in your life into a testimony?
2. How can you help guard the unity of God's people?
3. What witness does your community give that "the Lord is God"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You turn misunderstandings into monuments of grace. Help us to guard our unity and to be a living witness that You alone are God. Amen.
